intro: Mauritania is a desert country linking North and West Africa, home to ancient caravan towns and desert libraries.

chapters.title: Ghana Empire and Almoravids
text: Koumbi Saleh, in the south, may have been the capital of the old Ghana Empire. In the 1000s the Almoravid movement began here before conquering Morocco and Spain.

chapters.title: Caravan towns
text: Chinguetti, Ouadane, Tichitt and Oualata were stops on Saharan caravan routes. Chinguetti's family libraries still hold old manuscripts.

highlight.title: Chinguetti
highlight.text: Once called the 'seventh holy city of Islam' by some, it is a World Heritage site.

chapters.title: Colony and independence
text: France ruled Mauritania from the early 1900s. It became independent in 1960. Mauritania banned slavery in 1981, the last country to do so, and made it a crime in 2007, but rights groups say it still exists. Several coups have taken place; Mohamed Ould Ghazouani has been president since 2019.

timeline.title: Slavery abolished
timeline.text: The last country to do so.
